original_question: Construct, in ZFC and without extra set-theoretic hypotheses, general topological spaces, and also Lindelöf topological spaces, that witness non-implications among the classical selection properties shown in the paper's classification diagrams.
target_in_paper: Section 5, Project 1: "Find, without extra hypotheses, (general) topological spaces that demonstrate non-implications among the classical properties. Do the same for Lindelöf topological spaces."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the ZFC/no-extra-hypotheses setting, the two ambient classes explicitly requested in the paper (arbitrary topological spaces and Lindelöf topological spaces), and the goal of producing examples that witness failed implications among the paper’s classical selection properties from the classification section.
missing_details: The exact target is Section 5, Project 1, not the neighboring Problem 2 about a set of reals with the Menger property but not the Hurewicz property.
To be stand-alone, the question must define the underlying selection principles S1(U,V), Sfin(U,V), and Ufin(U,V).

It should specify the cover classes involved: O (open covers), Λ (open large covers), Ω (open ω-covers), and Γ (open γ-covers), and, if one wants full fidelity to Figure 2, also the countable Borel analogues B, BΛ, BΩ, and BΓ.
It should define what a cover means in this paper: a nontrivial cover U of X with X = ⋃U and X ∉ U.

It should define large, ω-, and γ-covers: each point belongs to infinitely many members; each finite subset is contained in some member; and the cover is infinite with each point in all but finitely many members, respectively.

It should make explicit that "demonstrate a non-implication" means: for a failed implication P ⇒ Q among the distinct classical properties in the classification, produce a space X such that X satisfies P but fails Q.
It should identify the relevant diagram as Figure 2, obtained after the standard equivalences and removals of duplicates described in Section 4 and Figure 1.

It should note the paper’s default convention that spaces are usually sets of reals unless otherwise indicated; this project is explicitly asking to go beyond that default to arbitrary topological spaces and then to the Lindelöf subcase.
refined_question: Let S1(U,V), Sfin(U,V), and Ufin(U,V) be the usual selection principles for classes of covers of a space X. Here a cover means a nontrivial cover U of X, i.e. X = ⋃U and X ∉ U; O, Λ, Ω, and Γ denote the families of open covers, open large covers, open ω-covers, and open γ-covers of X, respectively, and B, BΛ, BΩ, and BΓ denote the corresponding countable Borel-cover classes. Find, in ZFC alone and without any additional set-theoretic assumptions, arbitrary topological spaces, and separately Lindelöf topological spaces, that witness non-implications among the distinct classical selection properties appearing in Figure 2 of the paper; that is, for a failed implication P ⇒ Q among those classical properties, construct a space X with X satisfying P but not Q.
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s Section 5 Project 1 almost verbatim. The key clues are the explicit demand for ZFC examples, the emphasis on non-implications among the classical properties from the classification diagrams, and the separate request for arbitrary spaces and for Lindelöf spaces. Sections 2.1 and 3 supply the notation needed to make the question stand-alone, Section 4 explains that the relevant classical properties are the selection principles built from the cover classes in Figures 1 and 2, and Section 5 states the project itself. The paper does not contain items labeled Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, or Theorem 1.3, so Section 5, Project 1 is the nearest exact official formulation.
